e-8298.problem:
Which of the following statements are true?

- Any $1\times4$ matrix $A$ has at most $1$ singular value.

- Any $4\times2$ matrix $A$ has at most $2$ distinct singular values.

- The matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14078642/assets/a33b8a531dc91b49f01826cd7fcedaae2ee3144b5205bbe724efa9f29a302b37.png) has one negative singular value.
e-8298.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix $A^T \! A.$ 

With that in mind, let's examine our statements.

- Statement I is false. Since $A$ is a $1 \times 4$ matrix and $A^T$ is a $4\times 1$ matrix, $A^T \! A$ must be a $4 \times 4$ matrix: 

$$
\underset{\bbox[Gainsboro, 2pt]{\large 4} \times {\large 1}}{A^T} \times \underset{{\large 1} \times \bbox[Gainsboro, 2pt]{\large 4}}{A} =  
\underset{\bbox[Gainsboro, 2pt]{\large 4} \times \bbox[Gainsboro, 2pt]{\large 4}}{A^T \! A}
$$

Hence, $A$ has at most $4$ distinct singular values.

- Statement II is true. Since $A$ is a $4 \times 2$ matrix and $A^T$ is a $2\times 4$ matrix, $A^T \! A$ must be a $2 \times 2$ matrix: 

$$
\underset{\bbox[Gainsboro, 2pt]{\large 2} \times {\large 4}}{A^T} \times \underset{{\large 4} \times \bbox[Gainsboro, 2pt]{\large 2}}{A} = 
\underset{\bbox[Gainsboro, 2pt]{\large 2} \times \bbox[Gainsboro, 2pt]{\large 2}}{A^T \! A}
$$

Hence, $A$ has at most $2$ distinct singular values.

- Statement III is false. All singular values of any matrix are non-negative. So, $A$ cannot have a negative singular value.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

e-8299.knowledge_point: Finding the Singular Values of a Square Matrix
e-8299.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14078642/assets/9a78a1681842653fabade3354cc5e885f0bfc32eefa3b56e9d1faf716dc5d97b.png)
e-8299.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix $A^T \! A.$  

First, we calculate $A^T \! A\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 4 \\ 4 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of $A^T \! A\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}5-\lambda  & 4 \\ 4 & 5-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (5-\lambda )^{2}-16 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-10\lambda +9 & =0 \\ (\lambda -1)(\lambda -9) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =9,\,1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{9}=3 \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{1}=1\end{aligned}
$$

e-8300.knowledge_point: Finding the Singular Values of a Rectangular Matrix
e-8300.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14078642/assets/5d2eb1db497eeb2f3e24feaa1ac70547a48cc55d1eeea22da91231b1d1275df8.png)
e-8300.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix $A^T \! A.$  

First, we calculate $A^T \! A\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of $A^T \! A\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1-\lambda  & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 0 \\ 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}|+|\begin{aligned}0 & 1-\lambda  \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )(1-\lambda )^{2}-(1-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )((1-\lambda )^{2}-1) & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda ) & =0 \\ -\lambda (\lambda -1)(\lambda -2) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =2,\,1,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{2} \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{1}=1 \\ {\sigma }_{3} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{3}}=\sqrt{0}=0\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & \,\,-1 & 0 \\ 0 & \,\,-1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]?$
after.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}0 & \,\,-1 & 0 \\ 0 & \,\,-1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}0 & \,\,-1 & 0 \\ 0 & \,\,-1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 \\ \,\,-1 & \,\,-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & \,\,-1 & 0 \\ 0 & \,\,-1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2-\lambda  & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 0 \\ 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}|+|\begin{aligned}0 & 2-\lambda  \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )(2-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-(2-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )((1-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-1) & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda ) & =0 \\ \lambda (2-\lambda )^{2} & =0 \\ \lambda  & =2,\,2,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{2} \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{2} \\ {\sigma }_{3} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{3}}=\sqrt{0}=0\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}]?$
after.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -3 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10 & -6 \\ -6 & 10\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}10-\lambda  & -6 \\ -6 & 10-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (10-\lambda )(10-\lambda )-36 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-20\lambda +100-36 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-20\lambda +64 & =0 \\ (\lambda -4)(\lambda -16) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =16,\,4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{16}=4 \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{4}=2\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 \\ -1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 4 & -4 \\ -2 & -4 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}4-\lambda  & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 4-\lambda  & -4 \\ -2 & -4 & 5-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}4-\lambda  & -4 \\ -4 & 5-\lambda \end{aligned}|-2|\begin{aligned}0 & 4-\lambda  \\ -2 & -4\end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )((4-\lambda )(5-\lambda )-16)-4(4-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )(20-4\lambda -5\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}-16)-4(4-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-9\lambda +4)-4(4-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-9\lambda +4-4) & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-9\lambda ) & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -4)(\lambda -9) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =9,\,4,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

Question 6

What are the singular values of the matrix A=[12−1−2]?

a
10 and 0
b
10 and 2
c
3 and 2
d
10 and 0
e
3 and 0
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The singular values of the matrix A are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ATA.

First, we calculate ATA:

ATA=[12−1−2]T[12−1−2]=[1−12−2][12−1−2]=[2448]

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ATA:

|ATA−λI|=0|2−λ448−λ|=0(2−λ)(8−λ)−16=016−2λ−8λ+λ2−16=0λ2−10λ=0λ(λ−10)=0λ=10,0

Therefore, the singular values of A are as follows:

σ1=λ1=10σ2=λ2=0

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Singular Values of a Square Matrix
content.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}]?$
content.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 4 & 8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 4 \\ 4 & 8-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )(8-\lambda )-16 & =0 \\ 16-2\lambda -8\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}-16 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-10\lambda  & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -10) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =10,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{10} \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=0\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1-\lambda  & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1-\lambda  & 0\end{aligned}|+(1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 1 \\ 1 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ -(1-\lambda )+(1-\lambda )[(2-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-1)] & =0 \\ -(1-\lambda )+(1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-3\lambda +1) & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-3\lambda +1-1) & =0 \\ \lambda (1-\lambda )(\lambda -3) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =3,\,1,\,0\end{aligned}

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Singular Values of a Rectangular Matrix
content.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]?$
content.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1-\lambda  & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1-\lambda  & 0\end{aligned}|+(1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 1 \\ 1 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ -(1-\lambda )+(1-\lambda )[(2-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-1)] & =0 \\ -(1-\lambda )+(1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-3\lambda +1) & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-3\lambda +1-1) & =0 \\ \lambda (1-\lambda )(\lambda -3) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =3,\,1,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{3} \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{1}=1 \\ {\sigma }_{3} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{3}}=\sqrt{0}=0\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 4-\lambda  & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ -\lambda |\begin{aligned}4-\lambda  & 2 \\ 2 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ -\lambda [(1-\lambda )(4-\lambda )-4)] & =0 \\ -\lambda ({\lambda }^{2}-5\lambda +4-4) & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}(\lambda -5) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =5,\,0,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{5} \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{0}=0 \\ {\sigma }_{3} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{3}}=\sqrt{0}=0\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}]?$
content.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 4-\lambda  & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ -\lambda |\begin{aligned}4-\lambda  & 2 \\ 2 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ -\lambda [(1-\lambda )(4-\lambda )-4)] & =0 \\ -\lambda ({\lambda }^{2}-5\lambda +4-4) & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}(\lambda -5) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =5,\,0,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{5} \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{0}=0 \\ {\sigma }_{3} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{3}}=\sqrt{0}=0\end{aligned}
$$
